To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the unitary distance (10 nm) of myofilament shortening per ATP molecule (single myosin head) is independent of Pi and AD.

the myofilament distance of sliding induced by photoreleased ATP increases with the increase in ATP concentration, and the myofilament velocity of sliding induced by ATP increases with the decrease in the concentration of ATP.

the myofilament distance sliding induced by laser photolysis of ATP in glycerinated muscle fibres depends on the ATP concentration and that the effect of inorganics is consistent with the model of myofilament movement proposed in our previous paper (Matsuno et al. 2001).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanism of myosin head movement during myosin-actin interaction, and suggests that the myosin head can be divided into three states, namely AM, M and M.ADP, in which the state AM.ADP is the most important one for force generation.
the effects of Pi and ADPi on the myofilaments sliding induced by photoreleased ATP.
the effect of inorganics on the myofilaments sliding induced by photoreleased ATP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the unitary distance (10 nm) of myofilament slinding per ATP molecule is not changed by Pi and ADP, but the number of the unitary distance is increased by Pi and is decreased by ADP.

the myofilament movement induced by photoreleased ATP under nearly isometric condition is a result of the cooperative action of multiple myosin heads, and the myosin head force generating process is controlled by the chemical state of the actomyosin complex.

the myofilament shortening induced by photoreleased ATP can be explained by a simple model in which a single myosin molecule generates a force of 1.2 piconewton and moves 10 nm along an actin filament in each powerstroke, and the force is produced by the binding and hydrolysis of ATP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
myofilament sliding is regulated in a manner that is consistent with a two-state model for the cross-bridges.
the unitary powerstroke is 10 nm, and the number of powerstrokes per myosin head per ATP molecule is 2.5-5.0.
the myosin heads in the muscle fiber are not in the same state, and that the state of myosin heads is regulated by the concentration of ADP and Pi.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the unitary distance and the velocity of the myofilaments sliding induced by 10 mM Pi are larger than that induced by 0.4 mM ADP.
the unitary distance per ATP molecule is about 10.0 nm, and that the myofilament shortening velocity is proportional to the number of myosin heads that can generate force.
the unitary distance and velocity of the myofilaments sliding can be regulated by the population of myosin head intermediate states.
